name: The Ash-Baron Wilds
summary: The Ashlands' interior: a shifting map of salvage-camps, fortified farmsteads, and petty 'barons' who rule exactly as far as their riders can ride. There is no government, no law, and no shortage of order — the barons' code is simple: toll at the crossing, tribute to no one, and what the Sundering left belongs to whoever carries it out.

government.title: none
government.note: Roughly a dozen barons command riders; alliances last a season. The strongest, Baron Hesk of the Glass Road, mints no coins but his tokens spend.

population.note: runners between the wilds and the sands

laws: None written, none sworn. Custom: crossing-toll is sacred, water is shared, Glimmerborn are left alone (the wilds remember Solmere's refugees kindly), and Censer wagons are fair salvage.

relations.note: Barons pay crossing-toll and nothing else.
The town's market is the wilds' only safe commerce.
Seizure convoys get ambushed; ambushers get purged; repeat.

history_notes: The wilds sheltered Solmere's refugees after 183 AA — the barons' one point of pride.
Baron Hesk's riders were first on-site when the Karvess humming stopped. They will not say what they saw.
adventure_hooks: Players need a baron's riders as guides to Karvess; the price is stealing back a hostage from a rival baron.
A Censer wagon wreck litters the road with seized books; every faction wants them and the barons auction them at dawn.
An ash-farm village asks players to carry its tithe to Baron Hesk — and its real plea to the Crown.
